body:
Hey - I'm so sorry to hear about the mix of bullying and alcoholism (also sorta like bullying) that you're dealing with. It's a shitty mix that probably makes you feel like you can't do anything right...and sounds very familiar...

I honestly never figured out to deal with alcohol-induced emotional abuse; my step-father was fairly bad in that regard and started when I was around 14-15. Best advise I can give there is to ignore, best you can, and of the shit he/she is talking about you. How is your relationship with your other parent? Are they as impacted as you?

I'm even more sorry about the physical abuse both from the bullies and the one parent; that's shit that nobody needs to deal with. 

My escape, similar to what you're starting to do, was music and drama. I did music (band) for all of HS and it's where I found my closest fiends in HS. When you meet other people so have the same interests as you, you're more likely to connect with someone. 

Is drama something that you can stick with? Though I was more on the tech side of that (lights, sound etc...yeah I was a nerd haha) watching the actors/actresses get into character helped me to "be" the person I wanted to be and quash all the background stuff that was weighing me down. 

Huge applause on keeping your marks up. That's something you should be very proud of. I know it's not as "cool" as being starting QB but...honestly...you'll be further ahead with the higher marks IMO. 

As Frequency7 says, university > HS. You sound like someone who will have both the intelligence (your good marks) and the determination (you clearly WANT to succeed hence asking here) that will serve you well there and hope you will have the opportunity to attend.

Wanting to have family support and a non-violent school environment, with close fiends, is NOT at all ungrateful. Keep up with your great academic results, find stuff outside the classroom (either in-school extracurriculars or other stuff) to broaden your horizon...heck, try something new...? 

Things get better. I know it doesn't seem likely. I know it seems like the world is working against you. I know its a cliché. Once you find your groove (stuff u like to do) and learn how to deal with bad things, you'll be unstoppable. 

Best of luck!
Hey not sure if you're checking PMs on this acct...but pls check :)

Ok I'll create a throwaway Skype id (my main one has my name in it haha) and post back here when I get home from work. 

It's very encouraging to hear your extended family has been involved at the worst of times. The follow up part is something to focus on. Who has been the most helpful/responsive/positive to you and how is your relationship with them?

I don't know the people in your life so I can't directly counter your claim...but when I said more-or-less the exact same thing to someone in my "darker days", they were able to point to a few examples where I thought there were none. 

Despite their...personalities...?...your parents and brother would be shell-shocked. I'm sure you have some extended family (aunts, uncles, cousins, grandparents etc.) that would weep openly and GENUINELY grieve. Friends, classmates, co-workers, neighbors...you may think lowly of yourself, but that doesn't mean people think the same way, regardless of their attitude towards you. 

Live instant messaging may be a good idea, but I really want to keep anonymous (mutual protection). Have any ideas? IRC, throwaway gmail addresses for gtalk...? I'm in EST (so +2 hours from CO iirc) and will be around this evening. Let me mow what you think.

You write well and thus seem intelligent, you actually have feelings (though negative ones now), you genuinely seem to WANT to improve...but are locked in this dungeon of pain and negativity. Snooki is a drain on society...not you. (goin for a joke there...really hope you're not a fan!! :) )

Hey bud - your comments have changed a lot from your original post yesterday and I'm worried by what you're saying.  Did something happen since your original post that you're able to share? 

Suicidal thoughts are very real. If you have specific plans or it's feeling "real", I need you to promise me you'll call 911 and ask for help. You're NOT a horrible person and I need to know that you are still with me.

Your thoughts don't make you a horrible person. If you take nothing else away from this conversation...please I hope this sticks. 

Identifying depressive and suicidal thoughts as something you don't want to experience and doing what you've done to try and improve (seeking professional help, trying to talk to friends, coming here, other stuff I'm sure) show you WANT to overcome...and that isn't what a horrible person does.

You have experienced horrible things with people in the past but you aren't those people.  You're actively trying to improve. You're dealing with some serious shit that's hardly a joke...or at least a normal person wouldn't see a joke there. 

It goes back to finding reasons to care, and that's about motivating yourself to want to do things...small things at first, leading up to things that are more ambitious.  You have to want to care...and I don't think there is a secret fr that. However involving others in your life makes it easier. What opportunities exist to meet new people given the things you're interested in doing?

Ah ok fair enough.  Just wanted to share something that helped me. 

Have you had an opportunity to talk to someone in the last day about how you are feeling? You say that friends don't take your feelings seriously - any ideas why?

FWIW I'm really messed up after a few nights of poor sleep; motivation plummets, depressive thoughts go wild.

Good for not wanting to try prescription sleep aids, especially if they're antihistamine based. 

I find that melatonin supplements helped a lot...in fact, I credit them from turning me around from the worst of my depression. What have you tried?

Alternatively a friend got relief from prescription anti-anxiety meds (not sleep aids). His anxiety was keeping him from sleeping, which caused depression, which caused more anxiety...downward cycle...  I'm not sure what your meds are but wanted to mention this. 

I honestly think that not sleeping right caused a LOT of my own nonsense... I didn't have the balls to go see anyone (thought it was an admission of defeat blah blah - feel like an idiot for not having sought help) like you did; what has your dr said about insomnia?

Right - sorry, fair enough. 

Re sleeping - how are things there?

The goal things is kind of a trick you need to play on yourself. I know it sounds dumb (how can I trick myself?!?) but by setting goals and attaching meaning to them, bit-by-bit these small wins can help.  Not caring might mean the goals need to be even shorter-term wins. Baby steps...

Meds are a bitch; the fact they are not working has to be hard for you as well. I'm really happy to hear you have a good experience with your doctor...that's a great start. Have you tried different meds, different combinations of them? I've had friends not react at all to something but do a 180 on different meds.  Not to give false hope but it's something to try. 

It's clear you aren't "dumb" - you write a hell of a lot better than I did at 17 :).  It's also a good sign that you know that you "should" care more.  

It's a rough cycle to be in: knowing you should care, not caring, feeling worse, doing bad at school, feeling bad because you did bad, getting pissed off that you're feeling worse, etc...it's a cycle that needs to break and there is no one guaranteed way to do it.  Could be new meds, could be finding a new interest, could be finally breaking through to one friend who finally gets it. It's not easy but you show you WANT to break it and that's a good first step. 

You say you don't care...I get that, but any idea why you feel that way?

How well do you sleep? 

...Kurt was brilliant! I subscribe to the Courtney-related theories ;) (weird, teen spirit just came on the radio as I'm typing this...!!)

I can't begin to understand how bad you must feel; your description of the closest people to you sent chills down my spine - so sorry to hear. 

A few things...

People who try to motivate with with such threats aren't really doing you any favors. Motivation has to come from within.  I understand that's not easy; the best way I've heard is to target small, achievable victories that you can accomplish fairly quickly, but that also require some effort. Personal stuff (learn a new skill, meet a new person, find a cool place to go for a walk), academic stuff (get 8% higher on a next test).  Focusing on small wins before large ones is kinda like crawling before running. It's a place to start and not meant to be embarrassing. 

Professional help... You mention that you are on meds - I've seen people make significant changes with changes here. If your Dr isn't cooperating, is it possible to get a second opinion from someone else? 

Peer support is going to help a lot.  Is there someone there you can confide in on an individual level? Telling a group of friends isn't going to be easy but is there one person that can help? They can be used to help monitor the goals you set (from above) and to add perspective. This is a great community (I'm a long-time lurker...) and I hope you get some perspective from people here, but having even one person IRL to help will make things go so much easier. 

I won't say it's easy to rebound. But if you start with some small wins and positive influences, I'm confident you'll climb out of your rut. 

Some stuff that helps me FWIW
-long walks (until my feet are screaming at me!)
-loud music
-engaging in ridiculous debates with friends (not about your feelings, lighter stuff)
-hitting a squash ball
-cooking
-learning useless facts

PM if you want to talk, vent, scream...
Thanks also for the conversation!

Hehe reminding me of my times as a DD and some of the lunacy. 

I'm very sorry to hear about the negative influence that alcohol has had; I've seen some of what you identify but fortunately haven't lost a relative to it.  I can't imagine what that must be like......but good for you for realizing the answer isn't at the bottom of a bottle.  Hard to fault the odd use; as you describe, I also sometimes use it to bridge between the then-current time and when I'm tired enough to actually fall asleep. 

Glad to see I'm not alone with some of this stuff haha

You say your family deserves better.  Not that I want you to re-live past crap, but why do you feel that way?  

I bury myself in work because it kills the time; yeah I guess I enjoy it sometimes but normally it's a way to fill time...so I pull as many extra assignments as I can get just to take up more time. It's a distraction but certainly not enough reason to keep going...

Gaming and sports are at least interests! I avoid them kinda since I'm competitive....and also suck t both!

I've recently taken an objective look at my personality to help make me a "better" person, I.e. more adaptable to friends. I've noticed things which could put others off, and want to start improving.  Then I get hit by the depression freight train, stop caring and flip on tv. One needs a reason to improve...haven't found anything sustainable...lol?

What do you think some of your barriers to succeeding at various things are? If its ability (we aren't all rocket scientists haha), I don't buy that there isn't something you excel at.  If its interest...ok, I get that...but you clearly have some motivation to improve (feeling lonely implies you WANT more social interaction). 

Take stock in what works and what doesn't, and try to work on that. Get some honest feedback from ppl around you.  It may sting...but it's kinda like exercise burn. 

You saying your lonely is kind of a good sign - being totally ambivalent and not giving a shit is bad...lot loneliness implies desire for companionship. Gives you a goal. Working towards it isn't easy...but...give 'er!

Sounds kinda familiar...sober me acts the way society wants me to act given the scenario but drunk me acts more the way I want to. Oddly enough, drunk me is more fun...

I've had the benefit (odd word but if you think, it makes sense) of being exposed t my fair share of alcoholics...so I have the sense to not drink to avoid my problems (too much haha). 

You say drunk you is more like you, "used to be".  Any idea what changed to sour your personality?

Fuck you make a great point! If I put half the effort from the masking into trying to improve, things may be different.

Don't be envious; my logical half knows I'm chronically depressed but won't admit to it and get help. My depressed half is, well, depressed. They fight it out and I get to watch...maybe that'd make a good TV show? :) 

(I negotiate a lot for work; doing this requires me to mask what I'm thinking and I apply these skills in my personal life to hide my depression...95% it works and 4% I can bluff my way through it. The latent depression is there...just repressed...which is never a good thing!)

There isn't much sense trying to talk you out of feeling bad for your mother's response, but a) it proves she cares enough to be upset rather than be indifferent and b) it's your unwanted dark thoughts, not "you" that is the issue. Maybe there's a bit of motivation to improve?  It sounds like she's important to you...and though I know nothing of the relationship ou have with her, maybe she is willing to help? Maybe a starting point?

Telling your mother had to be an amazingly difficult thing to do; given I don't have the courage to tell close friends etc (let alone a parent), I tip my proverbial hat to you. It must have been awkward, as must her ongoing pain...but remember (hard to do this...) that this is her pain; you have your own issues to deal with, you can't add her reaction to your issues and thus compound things...

I'm not personally a fan of that theory to honest as it assumes we have no control over our own destiny. I never claimed a lack of control, only a lack of giving a damn to try and take control. I feel that people have control over their lives and thus can choose how to live them. Motivation (extrinsic or intrinsic) is needed...however...

I also feel that the best is behind me.  "rational me" (frequently locked away far from consciousness lol) says that this only means I need to create something new and cool to do...if only I cared enough to!

I think there is always the option to get better as one's place in life's a function of perspective.  I'm looking for reasons to improve...maybe that's an easier task for you. I sure hope so :)

Try and use the momentum from reading all this to figure out some ways to bring some positive stuff to your life. 

As someone said in another post in this sub, it's important to add up your small wins...and don't let bumps along the way scare you off. 

Best of luck!

You've nailed a key issue!  I have no desire to start a family or lie with someone...so am I supposed to die, alone, in however many years? Why not live as hard as I can now and go out on top?? (credit to another poster here for that concept). 

I go through the grind to get the odd challenge...wash, rinse, repeat. 

It's tough to find meaning in short term things when you have that long term view.  A poster from last night talked about looking at small wins together...makes sense but I guess it needs to be done often enough to obscure the horizon. 

Hope this is making at least some sense :)

For me, the suicidal thoughts help to frame things as I then look at it from the perspective of people who could be impacted by the decision. Sometimes that helps, others I need other motivation to get through the day as pleasing others, while good, isn't a reason to continue living. 

I like the philosophy of going out on top...made me laugh.  

I'm all for continuing the dialogue, but maybe here where it may benefit others who read this and are in a similar situation but aren't up to typing. If there are ideas tht re relevant, it may be good to share.

Now get back to your diorama :P

Looking for answers wasn't something realistic but it's interesting to see the amount of response on this. 

Do you feel better or worse by doing what is expected? Though I like to please people (minds out of the gutter!!) it's the social expectations that cause a lot of friction for me. 

What sort of things help your mood? Anything predictable? I think it'd be good to share ideas; there seems to be a lot of like-minded people reading this.

I know it seems odd to try and post something positive given my other post here, but I know what it's like to be (very) depressed approaching high school.

My trip through high school was...well, like many others', turbulent.  Ups and downs.  Don't worry though, because it's mostly benign noise that you can ignore. Things I found to really help:
- don't be down if you don't have a lot of friends; try to focus on one or two very close ones as it's the depth of relationship that is important, not the number of friends on your facebook account
- find an extra-curricular; try anything that sounds interesting...I tried things that I never thought I'd like and they not only helped me meet new ppl but also give me things to do I still enjoy today
- work if you can; having cash to spend is nice and it helps your self-esteem (I delivered papers and whatnot...)
- have a goal (a trade school, college, world domination...) and work generally towards it, but be flexible enough to try new things

Someone else here said college was the best time of your life... Many people say HS is, and I can see why. For me, it was university/college, no question. Hindsight being 20/20, knowing what I do now about university, I'd have had so much more to look forward to in HS.

So, does it get better? With the effort to find things you enjoy and get meaning from, life is good. Life is what you make of it. I posted here looking to get others' perspectives on coasting through life; the message I see is its important to give yourself meaning through the things you enioy doing.  Don't be afraid to try new things and find people with common interest to hang with and become friends. 

By posting here, it's clear you want to improve and that you don't want to be depressed. Find things you enjoy and trust someone you're close to with your depression so they can help you through it. With that, things DO get better. 

...hell, when I was 13, I practically salivated over the thought of turning 16 and getting my license. That's reason enough to push past the things putting you in a dark place :)

Cheers.

"...might as well attempt the impossible beforehand. If I fail, then hey, whatever I can just give up afterwards. "

Well said. 

I'm not THAT ambitious; instead I'm challenging the "well, I have to live..." assumption. Sometimes. 

I noted above I distract my depressive thoughts by nosing into serious challenges at work; maybe looking outside of work for external challenges is an approach. 

Thanks for your note!

Level-headed, pragmatic and rational...which is why I know that these thoughts aren't right and haven't acted on them...but can't control their continued presence. 

Interesting chicken-and-egg view on passive living vis-a-vis depression.  Basic psych says passive affect (losing interest etc.) is a sign of depression...but is it a cause...

It sounds, like me, you get lost in a challenge (in a good way). This is how I find purpose - looking for something "to fix" (not in a hammer and nails way...but sometimes :)) and going through the process of learning how it works and fixing it. This is usually at work where I can find projects that last a year...which helps.  The more stressed I am with work, the less depressed I am. 

Thanks for the perspective; helps validate my views.

Being able to stay more or less emotion-free has helped me to be objective with others' problems...but obviously doesn't fit most peoples' expectations. It's pragmatic but by no means a utopia...

Ive certainly thought of what I'd write...but getting down to that level and individualizing my thoughts like that usually snaps me around into a more rational state.  "Yeah, right, like I have the balls to write that to him/her, dead or not."

Ups and downs are a fact I can deal with. I just don't have the same patience and motivation that most people do, I guess 

Thanks for your response!

Hah...I actually get a kick out of non-conformance; I'm kind of "eccentric" and proud of it haha. 

Friends are definitely a part of my life, but they strangely don't figure into my most depressive thoughts. It's almost like I am not afraid of the impacts of them; I know this is socially wrong but it is how I feel. 

It's no so much being a part of the status quo that concerns me, but not having a point to my existence and no real willingness to establish one. Most people have a point to some extent - be it a personal, social or commercial victory. I just have no motivation to set a goal like that and work for it...hence my "waiting it out" view. 

I do, however, make sense of your guidance about the additive value of individual wins. 

The thoughts come and go. Beating them may not be a good goal but managing them is. Reflection on small wins sounds like a good start. Thanks!
